blast_radius.contracts_and_data: Additive, optional keys inside the existing runtime_tasks.budget_json document; no new table, store file or SQLite schema version is planned. Limits are emitted only when declared, so the budget identity hashed by runtime_persistence.compute_task_budget_identity is unchanged for every existing task and mission binding, while declaring a new limit is an authority-changing budget update that invalidates captured bindings as today. Cancellation and bounded-stop evidence goes to the existing runtime_task_transitions evidence_json. No artifact bytes, prompts or secrets are stored; reports carry identifiers, digests, counts and durations only.
blast_radius.authority_and_resources: No credential, provider or model inference, network egress, browser worker, account, billable action, background process or new filesystem grant. Mission cancellation needs the typed server-created AP-004 MissionAuthorityEnvelope, never request JSON or model arguments. Memory and storage readings are supplied by the caller or measured read-only on already-owned processes and confined paths; an unavailable reading for a declared limit stops the work rather than assuming headroom. Isolation that is absent, unqualified, stale or under incident refuses dependent execution and never selects the host shell.
blast_radius.compatibility_and_rollback: Existing budget documents parse unchanged and keep their identity digest; a task without the new limits behaves exactly as before. Rollback is a source revert: an older binary ignores unknown optional keys only if none were written, so the candidate must prove with a test what an older reader does with a document that carries the new keys, and document that outcome instead of assuming it. No data is deleted, no destructive reset is used, and cancel/stop transitions append history rather than rewrite it.
blast_radius.required_evidence: Positive and negative tests for mission cancellation (dispatch refused afterwards, owned fixture subprocesses terminated, one measured cleanup latency recorded); stale and race tests (late completion, late checkpoint and late spawn after cancel are fenced; a second cancel is idempotent); uncertain consequential effects stay uncertain and block completion until reconciled; bounded stops for no-progress, repeated repair, deadline, memory and storage including the unavailable-measurement case and restart persistence of the committed stop reason; isolation-absent refusal with proof that no host execution path ran; truthful report tests proving a stopped mission never reads as succeeded and lists retained partial artifacts with a limitation; budget-identity compatibility for existing documents; existing budget, mission, supervision, side-effect, sandbox, recovery-guard and artifact-lineage regressions; static checks and generated-artifact drift.

scope_deviations: Live paths: the claim described an offline subset. Most of the work is unreachable until a caller is added, but not all of it. Three fail-closed changes are on paths the running application already uses: a late result no longer settles an action the ledger already marked uncertain (all tasks, not only missions); the budget charge reads every budget from the task to the root; and /api/harness/run and /api/harness/gsd-wave answer 400 for the six new budget keys. Each change only adds a refusal. The first one changes existing behaviour in one race: a session whose action was marked uncertain by a cancel, takeover or recovery while its executor was still running now pauses for reconciliation instead of continuing with the late result.

Scope reading: this candidate adds behaviour to six production modules, not tests only. The U06 safe work line reads “implement offline refusal, cancellation and uncertain-effect tests”, and docs/autonomous-production-u06-call-path-audit.md (PR #304, merged to main after this claim) takes the position that those tests should wait for the U06 decision and a story authorization (its gap G-6). The claim's pre-edit blast radius did announce the implementation, and the Relay rule allows a safe fail-closed subset of a blocked story. The owner decides which reading stands; this record does not.

Stop evidence location: blast_radius.contracts_and_data said cancellation and bounded-stop evidence goes to runtime_task_transitions evidence_json. Per-task transitions do record the mission, plan version, stop kind, stop code and unresolved action ids, but the measured stop record (latency, survivors, fences) is stored in mission_recovery report rows in the existing runtime_mission_joins table. No table, column, store file or schema version was added.

Files: execution_spine.py (late_result_fenced at the action boundary) and app.py (isolation_unavailable denial; HTTP 400 for the six new budget keys) were changed although the pre-edit list did not name them. sandbox_boundary.py, recovery_guard.py and artifact_lineage.py were anticipated and not changed.

HTTP behaviour: no route was added or removed, but /api/harness/run and /api/harness/gsd-wave now answer 400 when the budget object names max_no_progress, max_repair_attempts, deadline_at, max_memory_bytes, max_storage_bytes or isolation_required. The parser ignored unknown keys before, so a client sending one of these names was accepted and is now refused. No caller in this repository sends them.
Tests: no dedicated AP-007 test module was added. The 55 cases live in five existing modules, so the CI shard map and test scope map are unchanged.

Older-reader proof: blast_radius.compatibility_and_rollback said a test must prove what an older reader does with the new keys. A repository test cannot import the previous release's reader, so the outcome was measured once against the base commit's module and documented as a rollback hazard instead.

Reuse: recovery_guard was not reused for no-progress and repair limits, because its task identifiers cannot hold mission task ids; the counters live in the budget document. cancel_task keeps its one-level cascade; a whole-task cancel with an active mission is cancel_task(root) followed by halt_mission.
